results.evidence: Forest Service pages for the Twin Lakes trailhead and Mt. Baker Wilderness list only a recreation pass and wilderness rules (party of 12); the forest-wide regulations page says visitors 'may need' a free self-issue permit at some trailheads without naming Mt. Baker Wilderness. The statewide backcountry-permit page likewise names no requirement for this wilderness, and the peak's own route page (Red Tape section) could not be fetched (403). Would settle it: a Mt. Baker Ranger District statement naming whether a self-issue permit is required here.

Retry found no new car-to-summit figure for the Andrews Creek approach: the only new stated total (5,600 ft for a 42-mile trip taking in both Cathedral Peak and Amphitheater) covers two summits and cannot be split, and other pages give only approach gains to the lakes (4,200-4,600 ft) or an overall trip total of 13,500 ft for both peaks. The row's own trailhead (3,050 ft) and summit (8,358 ft) prove the stored figure is too low, but no two sources state one car-to-summit total. Would settle it: two independent trip logs via Andrews Creek stating the same round-trip gain. loss_ft (4800) has the same problem and was left unchanged.

results.fact: Which side of the lake to walk around
results.correct_value: West side (from camps on the north shore)
results.evidence: The route's own page says that when camped on the north side of Upper Cathedral Lake you walk around the lake on the west side and up to the buttress (~15 min), matching approach_variants; the stored approach text appears to have merged 'camped on the north side' into the walking direction, and the buttress pins sit south of the lake. No second independent source naming the side could be read (the area page says only to approach from Upper Cathedral Lake or Cathedral Pass; the magazine write-up is behind a login). Would settle it: one more independent approach description naming the west shore.
